Use case: compositing. Image 1 is the exact original adult game portrait and the authority for every visible accessory, hairstyle, expression, clothing detail, lighting and composition. Image 2 is the yellow mascot anatomy and identity reference. Generate one new independent full-resolution mascot portrait from these two inputs.
Rebuild the character with the smooth compact rounded yellow mascot head and green-ringed black eyes of image 2. The entire central face between the eyeglass hardware and moustache is one smooth broad continuous curved surface: there is no independent nose bridge, triangular nose wedge, nose tip, nostrils, human ears or human skin. The spectacles have their own separate black metal bridge and small gold fittings; those are hardware resting against the smooth face. The source human nose anatomy is replaced along with all other source human facial anatomy.
Retain the exact adult source's tall voluminous swept curly dark-brown/grey hair, two independent dark hair eyebrows, dark round spectacles with small gold fittings and lens reflections, and the short brown-grey moustache with its actual visible outline. Preserve one small serious closed or very slightly parted mascot mouth below the moustache matching the source expression; no second mouth, fleshy lip rolls or invented beard. Keep the original slight screen-left three-quarter head turn, gaze, chest-up crop and upper-left lighting.
Retain the brown broad-lapel coat, white pointed shirt collar, red-and-ochre diagonally striped tie and their actual crop and visible details. Fit the collar and shoulders around the mascot's compact round chin with a very short broad neck transition. Preserve the existing fastening and neckline, with no long yellow neck column, pinched collar ring, floating fabric, clipping or cream neck bib. Keep the whole original dark grey-brown painted rectangular background and original clothing through all four image edges; everything is opaque, including glasses, hair, dark fabric and all background corners. No new photograph frame, note, symbol, person, readable label, watermark or comparison panels. Preserve the original portrait aspect ratio and full generated detail.
